correctness.rationale: The two Chebyshev square identities make the translated equation u²−f²h. The factor y−1 has odd valuation in h, so the quadratic extensions are domains. With A=C[y,z], R=A⊕fAw sits in B=A⊕Aw, w²=h, by u=fw; B is integral and finite, and inversion of f identifies the fraction fields. The singular locus of B is exactly the four transverse simultaneous zeros of y²−1 and z²−1 with w=0. Thus this hypersurface satisfies R₁ and S₂, and a=yz+w identifies it with the stated Cayley cubic. To be in the conductor r=a+fbw must satisfy rw∈R, exactly f|a; hence fB=(f,u), and B/R≅A/(f) as A-modules. The U-polynomial roots are simple, all off ±1, for every index including 2. Off f=0 the four isolated nodes persist; on f=0 all singular points have u=0. In the completions each unit square root can be absorbed. The formal types are obtained by one simple f factor, two f factors, one f and one h factor, or two h factors with f a unit; this exhausts the loci. The intrinsic ideal is the second Fitting ideal of differentials. In pinch and crossing models its radical quotient is generated by v and vw respectively, killed by the closed-point maximal ideal and nonzero, giving length one at each; the ordinary double and node ideals are radical. The connected incidence graph has unique bipartition up to reversal, including the 1×1 case, so its unordered part sizes recover the indices, and swapping y,z gives the converse.
residual_risks: Formal local branches are not global components of the surface or its normalization cover. Characteristic-zero square roots and the complex simple-root description are used; this does not give a smooth resolution.

evidence: The 2025 parametrization for columns e₁,e₂,(m,n), phase zero, is (y,z,x)=(cos s,cos t,cos(ms+nt)) in cosine notation. In multiplicative coordinates the first two cosines give four possible sign/inversion choices in a generic fiber; the mixed cosine identifies only simultaneous inversion for all positive m,n. Coordinatewise monic quadratics make the torus map finite.
Proposition 5.8 in the 2024 article supplies a candidate singular-support containment, and the inspected exact examples cover S₂,₃ and S₃,₅ at reduced-support level.
broader_coverage.reasoning: The normal finite quotient (C*)² by simultaneous inversion is birational to the image. Its invariants y,z,a=(st+(st)^{-1})/2 in multiplicative coordinates give the Cayley cubic. Thus the common normalization is an immediate implication of the broader parametrization and standard invariant-ring reasoning, without a coprimality restriction. This does not specify the image conductor or the local embedded Jacobian ideals.

originality.rationale: Pass for the actual combined all-index theorem that computes the conductor and normalization quotient and describes the full formal/Jacobian stratification and isomorphism classification. Do not credit the common normalization alone as new: it follows by the elementary simultaneous-inversion quotient of the earlier torus parametrization, and is explicitly covered on the coprime subfamily by an adjacent same-day record. Known reduced-support results and the classical Cayley equation are also not new. The available statements do not calculate or imply merely by specialization the precise conductor and the embedded scheme excess that make this combined result distinct.
residual_risks: No priority inference from the same-day symmetric-phase match. Neither the torus-origin normalization nor the published reduced special cases should be counted separately as new.
The literature check is bounded; an earlier exact quadratic-order conductor or local-image classification for this family is not excluded.

value.rationale: The problem asks what remains of two frequency indices as intrinsic invariants when all surfaces share the same normalization. The exact conductor locates nonnormality and quantifies the quotient, the formal and Jacobian ideals distinguish different points on a common reduced grid, and the entire incidence structure recovers the unordered frequencies. These answer geometric questions that the normal quotient and a list of reduced curve components do not answer on their own.
residual_risks: Not a general deformation-theory result or smooth desingularization; value rests on the combined exact scheme and invariant analysis.
